name: Irish Stew
description: Real Irish stew is genuinely simpler than most recipes suggest - an actual Irish home cook is explicit that Worcestershire sauce is not authentic (an English condiment, not part of the dish's humble origins), and that no seasoning beyond a bay leaf, salt, and pepper is needed. Real technique uses lamb neck or shoulder specifically for its real collagen, which breaks down over the long simmer into a naturally silky, thickened broth - a leaner cut like leg would dry out before that happens. Guinness is a genuinely popular modern addition, not a traditional one.

ingredients_full.note: formed into chunks, standing in for neck or shoulder

ingredients.note: formed into chunks, standing in for neck or shoulder

steps_detailed: Add the onion and cook 3-4 minutes.

Add the carrot, potato, bay leaf, and enough water to just cover, and simmer 1.5-2 hours, until the lamb is genuinely fall-apart tender and the broth has thickened naturally - real Irish stew needs nothing more added than this.

name: Irish Colcannon
description: Colcannon, mashed potato worked together with real kale or cabbage and a generous knob of butter, is the real traditional side for Irish stew, though given the potatoes already in the stew itself, it's genuinely optional rather than essential.
steps_detailed: Boil the cabbage until tender, 8-10 minutes, then drain and chop finely.
Mash the potato with the butter and milk, being genuinely generous with the butter.

name: Irish Soda Bread
description: Irish soda bread, real brown wholemeal soda bread specifically, is the traditional accompaniment for pressing into Irish stew's broth, real technique using baking soda rather than yeast for its distinctive quick, dense crumb.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour, baking soda, and salt, then stir in the milk until just combined into a soft, shaggy dough - real technique avoids overworking it.
Shape into a round, score a cross on top, and bake at 425F (220C) for 25-28 minutes until deeply golden and firm.

name: Irish Boxty (Potato Pancake)
description: Boxty, a real potato pancake made from both raw grated and cooked mashed potato together, is a genuine Irish staple, real technique squeezing the raw grated potato well so the pancakes fry crisp.

ingredients_full.note: half raw grated, half boiled and mashed

ingredients.note: half raw grated, half boiled and mashed

steps_detailed: Squeeze the raw grated potato well to remove excess liquid.
Mix with the mashed potato and flour into a soft batter.
Fry spoonfuls, flattening slightly, 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden and crisp.

name: Irish Bacon and Cabbage
description: Bacon and cabbage, real ham simmered with cabbage, is a genuine Irish comfort staple, real technique simmering the cabbage in the same pot as the bacon so it absorbs real flavor.
steps_detailed: Simmer the bacon with the onion in 1.5 cups water 15 minutes.
Add the cabbage and simmer 12-15 minutes more, until tender and infused with the bacon's flavor.

name: Irish Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with butter and lemon, reflecting Ireland's rich Atlantic coastal fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the butter and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Irish Roasted Almonds
description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across Ireland.
steps_detailed: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

name: Irish Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Irish home cooking outside the specific named lamb-based dishes.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.
